title: Retrieving from Your Own Mistakes: On-Policy Training of Embedding Models for Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation
title_zh: 从自身错误中检索：面向多跳检索增强生成的嵌入模型在线策略训练

paragraphs.en: Complex questions in retrieval-augmented generation require evidence spread over several documents, and an answer is reliable only when the retriever finds all of it. Chain embedding retrievers collect such evidence step by step, re-encoding the question together with the passages retrieved so far, and we find that they are already strong: trained only on gold histories, a small chain embedding retriever that calls no language model outperforms graph-based systems and is competitive with a search agent. This training, however, leaves a gap. At test time the retriever conditions on its own retrievals, which soon contain mistakes: by the third step, about half or more of the states it visits hold a wrong passage, and these passages lower its chance of retrieving a missing gold passage well beyond what the difficulty of the states explains. We propose on-policy state training, which trains the encoder on the states it reaches itself. At every epoch the current encoder retrieves chains for the training questions; each state it visits, including those built on its own mistakes, is labeled with the earliest gold passage still missing while the other missing gold passages are masked, so that no correct continuation is penalized; and the encoder is updated contrastively on these states mixed with teacher-forced ones, so that its training distribution follows it as it learns. The resulting retriever retrieves complete evidence more often than teacher-forced training and the systems we compare, and it transfers without further training to harder long-chain variants of HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA that we construct. On the same states, it recovers from its own mistakes far more often, and controlled comparisons attribute the gain to training on the states the encoder currently reaches. Code and benchmarks are available at https://github.com/yausankit/on-policy-state-training .

paragraphs.en: Retrieval-augmented generation grounds a language model in retrieved documents ( Lewis et al., 2020 ) , and on the Web it lets search engines and assistants answer questions from large collections of pages that change faster than any model can be retrained. For complex questions the evidence is spread over several passages, and a missing passage is often enough to make the answer wrong ( Trivedi et al., 2022 ) . Two families of systems address this setting. One places a language model in the retrieval loop, either to reason between searches ( Jin et al., 2025 ) or to organize the corpus as a graph in advance ( Gutiérrez et al., 2025 ) . The other trains an embedding model to retrieve in a chain: at each step it encodes the question together with the passages found so far and retrieves the next one ( Xiong et al., 2021a ) . Chain embedding retrievers need no language model call and a single dense index, which makes them a practical first stage for Web-scale corpora, and a better one also helps systems of the first family.

paragraphs.en: A chain retriever is trained on one kind of history and used on another. During training, the passages in its history are gold passages, and the target is the next gold passage ( Xiong et al., 2021a ) . At test time the history consists of whatever the retriever itself retrieved. As soon as one of these passages is wrong, it stays in the query for every later step, and the retriever faces a state it was never trained on. Such states are common. On four-hop MuSiQue questions, 70% of the states that a teacher-forced chain retriever visits at its third step, and 89% at its fourth, already contain a non-gold passage (Section 3 ). In such states the retriever retrieves a missing gold passage 28% of the time, against 67% when its history is clean. Part of this gap reflects harder states, but deleting the wrong passages from the same states shows that they alone cost the retriever 11 points (Section 5.4 ). We call this the state mismatch. Chain dense retrievers trained with supervised targets use teacher forcing, and those that learn from their own trajectories rely on outcome rewards ( Sorokin et al., 2026 ) . Work on dense retrieval has improved the candidate side of training, through harder or cleaner negatives ( Xiong et al., 2021b ; Qu et al., 2021 ) , while the query-side histories remain gold.

paragraphs.en: To answer them we propose on-policy state training, which trains the encoder on the states that it reaches itself. In every epoch the current encoder retrieves chains for the training questions, and the states it visits, including those built on its own mistakes, replace half of the training states. Each visited state is labeled with the earliest gold passage that is still missing, while the other missing gold passages are masked so that retrieving any of them is never penalized; this target is defined by the gold set alone, so states with wrong passages receive the same dense supervision as gold states. Because the visited states are re-collected as the encoder changes, the training distribution follows the retriever as it learns. Everything else, from the architecture and the loss to the negatives and the document index, is shared with teacher-forced training, which isolates the distribution of training states. It also differs from methods that learn retrieval from outcome rewards ( Sorokin et al., 2026 ; Jin et al., 2025 ) , which need sparse rewards over whole episodes. We evaluate on MuSiQue and, to test whether the effect persists on longer chains and larger corpora, on harder variants of HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA that we construct ( Yang et al., 2018 ; Ho et al., 2020 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 为回答这些问题，我们提出在策略状态训练（on-policy state training），它在智能体自身到达的状态上训练编码器。 在每个轮次中，当前编码器为训练问题检索链条，它访问的状态（包括基于自身错误构建的状态）会替换一半的训练状态。 每个被访问的状态都以仍然缺失的最早的金标（gold）篇章作为标签，而其余缺失的金标篇章被掩蔽，因此检索到其中任何一个都不会受到惩罚；该目标仅由金标集合定义，因此包含错误篇章的状态与金标状态一样受到同等的稠密监督。 由于被访问的状态会随编码器的变化而重新收集，训练分布会跟随检索器的学习过程而变化。 其余所有部分，从架构、损失函数到负样本和文档索引，都与教师强制（teacher-forced）训练相同，从而将训练状态的分布隔离为唯一变量。 它也不同于从结果奖励中学习检索的方法（Sorokin et al., 2026; Jin et al., 2025），后者需要在整个回合上使用稀疏奖励。 我们在 MuSiQue 上进行评估，并在更长的链条和更大的语料库上检验该效果是否持续，为此我们构建了 HotpotQA 和 2WikiMultiHopQA 的更难变体（Yang et al., 2018; Ho et al., 2020）。

paragraphs.en: Questions that require several pieces of evidence are usually answered by retrieving in multiple rounds. One line of work places a large language model in the loop and learns when and what to search through reinforcement learning ( Jin et al., 2025 ) . Graph-based methods organize the corpus offline instead, as a knowledge graph traversed with personalized PageRank ( Gutiérrez et al., 2025 ) , a subgraph selected with a prize-collecting Steiner tree ( He et al., 2024 ) , or a relation-free entity graph ( Zhuang et al., 2026 ) . Our method calls no language model at retrieval time and uses only a dense passage index. The two directions are complementary, since a stronger embedding model can serve as the retriever inside either kind of system. An embedding retriever can also be trained from the outcome of a whole episode: Q-RAG learns a value-based embedder for multi-step retrieval from temporal-difference targets ( Sorokin et al., 2026 ) . Search-R1 and Q-RAG learn from sparse outcome rewards. Our method derives a dense per-step target from the gold evidence set, so every visited state is labeled without reward estimation, and neither training nor retrieval calls a language model.
paragraphs.zh: 需要多条证据的问题通常需要通过多轮检索来回答。 一类工作将大语言模型置于循环中，通过强化学习（Jin et al., 2025）学习何时搜索以及搜索什么。 基于图的方法则是在离线阶段组织语料库，例如构建为通过个性化 PageRank 遍历的知识图谱（Gutiérrez et al., 2025）、用带奖赏收集的 Steiner 树选择的子图（He et al., 2024），或无关系的实体图（Zhuang et al., 2026）。 我们的方法在检索时不调用任何语言模型，且仅使用稠密段落索引。 这两个方向是互补的，因为更强的嵌入模型可以作为其中任一类系统内部的检索器。 嵌入检索器也可以从整个回合的结果中训练：Q-RAG 从时序差分目标中学习用于多步检索的基于价值的嵌入器（Sorokin et al., 2026）。 Search-R1 和 Q-RAG 从稀疏的结果奖励中学习。 我们的方法从金标准证据集中推导出稠密的逐步目标，因此每个被访问的状态都无需奖励估计即被标注，且训练和检索均不调用语言模型。

paragraphs.en: Chain dense retrievers condition each hop on the passages retrieved at earlier hops. MDR concatenates the question with the previously retrieved passages and encodes the result with a shared dense encoder, trained with teacher forcing: the history at hop t t consists of gold passages, the target is the next gold passage, and negatives come from a memory bank of passage vectors ( Xiong et al., 2021a ) . Its training queries therefore never contain a passage the retriever retrieved by mistake, and no target is defined for a history that does. We keep the MDR-style chain architecture and a fixed document index, and change only the distribution of histories on which the query encoder is trained.
paragraphs.zh: 链式密集检索器在每一跳都以先前各跳检索到的段落为条件。 MDR 将问题与先前检索到的段落拼接，并用共享的密集编码器对结果进行编码，训练时采用教师强制：第 t 跳（hop t）的历史由标准（gold）段落组成，目标是下一个标准段落，负例来自段落向量的记忆库（Xiong et al., 2021a）。 因此，其训练查询中从不包含检索器错误检索到的段落，而对于包含错误段落的历史也没有定义目标。 我们保留了 MDR 式的链式架构和固定的文档索引，只改变了用于训练查询编码器的历史的分布。

paragraphs.en: Dense retrievers are trained contrastively on question–passage pairs ( Karpukhin et al., 2020 ) , and much of the progress comes from better negatives. ANCE re-encodes the corpus with the current checkpoint so that negatives follow the model’s own retrieval distribution ( Xiong et al., 2021b ) , and RocketQA removes false negatives with a cross-encoder ( Qu et al., 2021 ) . Contriever and recent embedding models built on large language models scale up pretraining ( Izacard et al., 2022 ; Lee et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ) . These methods improve the candidate side of the contrastive objective. Our method acts on the query side: it refreshes the retrieval states that the encoder embeds as queries, while the negatives stay those of the frozen encoder.
paragraphs.zh: 稠密检索器在问题—段落对上进行对比训练（Karpukhin et al., 2020），而大部分进展来自更好的负例。 ANCE 使用当前检查点重新编码语料库，使负例遵循模型自身的检索分布（Xiong et al., 2021b），而 RocketQA 则用交叉编码器去除假负例（Qu et al., 2021）。 Contriever 以及基于大语言模型构建的近期嵌入模型则扩大了预训练规模（Izacard et al., 2022；Lee et al., 2025；Zhang et al., 2025）。 这些方法改进的是对比目标的候选侧。 我们的方法作用于查询侧：它刷新编码器嵌入为查询的检索状态，而负例保持为冻结编码器的负例。

paragraphs.en: Training a sequential predictor only on reference histories, while it conditions on its own predictions at test time, is known as exposure bias ( Ranzato et al., 2016 ) . Imitation learning and sequence modeling address it by training on states the model itself visits ( Daumé III et al., 2009 ; Ross et al., 2011 ; Bengio et al., 2015 ) . DAgger rolls in with the learner and labels the visited states with an expert, and dynamic oracles define such an expert for every state of a dependency parser, including states off the gold path ( Goldberg and Nivre, 2012 ) ; AggreVaTe and LOLS label states with costs to go instead ( Ross and Bagnell, 2014 ; Chang et al., 2015 ) . The idea has recently been applied to language model agents ( Li et al., 2026 ; Liao et al., 2026 ) . Our training procedure is an instance of DAgger with a dynamic oracle. What we study is specific to chain dense retrieval: the oracle is free because the gold evidence set labels every state, a wrong passage persists in the query for all later steps, and only the query side of a contrastive objective changes. A related line makes language models robust to irrelevant retrieved context by training with distractors ( Yoran et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2024 ) ; Section 5.5 compares visited states with synthetic contamination of this kind.

paragraphs.en: We measure it with a chain retriever trained by teacher forcing on MuSiQue (gold histories drawn as random subsets), run for T = 4 T=4 steps on the 1,000 test questions. We count only feasible states: those at step t ≤ n t\leq n of an n n -hop question that still miss a gold passage, since for t > n t>n a missing gold passage implies a wrong one. On four-hop questions, 19% of the states at the second step, 70% at the third and 89% at the fourth already contain a non-gold passage; on three-hop questions the share is 12% at the second step and 48% at the third (Figure 3 a). paragraphs.en: MuSiQue ( Trivedi et al., 2022 ) is built so that its two- to four-hop questions cannot be answered from a single passage, which makes the history of a chain retriever matter at every step. All trained retrievers are trained on 1,800 MuSiQue training questions and select checkpoints on 200 others. We test on the 1,000 questions of the official development set with the 11,656-passage corpus used by HippoRAG 2 ( Gutiérrez et al., 2025 ) . To test whether the effect persists on longer chains and larger corpora, we evaluate the MuSiQue-trained encoders, without further training, on two harder benchmarks that we construct from HotpotQA ( Yang et al., 2018 ) and 2WikiMultiHopQA ( Ho et al., 2020 ) . HotpotQA-Long extends bridge questions along hyperlinks in the Wikipedia abstracts to chains of three, four and five pages (100 test questions each) over a corpus of 554,812 passages. 2Wiki-Long follows functional relations between Wikidata entities for three to five hops, or compares three to four entities that are each reached in two hops, with 300 test questions over 220,000 passages. In both benchmarks the question names only the starting entity, a language model of a different family verifies that the question is answerable from the gold passages and has a unique answer, and questions whose final passage is retrievable by BM25 from the question alone are removed. The corpora contain the lexical nearest neighbors of every gold passage, so distractors are topically close to the evidence (Appendix E ).
paragraphs.zh: MuSiQue（Trivedi 等，2022）的构建方式使其二跳至四跳的问题无法仅凭单一文段回答，这使得链式检索器的历史记录在每一步都很重要。 所有被训练的检索器都在 1,800 个 MuSiQue 训练问题上进行训练，并在另外 200 个问题上选择检查点。 我们在官方开发集的 1,000 个问题上进行测试，语料库为 HippoRAG 2（Gutiérrez 等，2025）所使用的 11,656 个文段。 为了检验这种效果在更长的推理链和更大的语料库上是否持续存在，我们在两个更难的基准上评估经 MuSiQue 训练的编码器（未做进一步训练），这两个基准由 HotpotQA（Yang 等，2018）和 2WikiMultiHopQA（Ho 等，2020）构建而成。 HotpotQA-Long 将维基百科摘要中的桥接问题沿超链接扩展为三、四、五页的推理链（各 100 个测试问题），语料库包含 554,812 个文段。2Wiki-Long 追踪 Wikidata 实体之间三到五跳的功能关系，或比较各自经过两跳到达的三到四个实体，共 300 个测试问题，语料库包含 220,000 个文段。 在这两个基准中，问题只指明起始实体，由一个不同系列的智能体验证该问题可以从金标文段中回答且答案唯一，并且那些仅凭问题本身就能通过 BM25 检索到最终文段的问题会被移除。 语料库包含每个金标文段的词汇最近邻，因此干扰项在主题上与证据十分接近（附录 E）。

paragraphs.en: BM25 and the frozen Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B encoder ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) retrieve with the question alone (Dense). HippoRAG 2 ( Gutiérrez et al., 2025 ) builds a knowledge graph with a language model and retrieves with personalized PageRank; we run the official code with the same frozen encoder. G-Retriever ( He et al., 2024 ) selects a subgraph of this knowledge graph with a prize-collecting Steiner tree; we rank the passages linked to the selected nodes and edges first. paragraphs.en: Table 1 supports the first finding. On MuSiQue, on-policy state training reaches 73.5 R@5 and 49.3 C@5. Search-R1, which reasons with a 7B language model between three searches on average, completes 36.5% of the questions within five passages, Q-RAG 36.2%, the released MDR checkpoint 31.9%, and HippoRAG 2, which calls a language model to build its graph, 23.1%. Most of the gain over the frozen encoder comes from training a chain retriever at all; the part due to the training states is isolated in Section 5.3 , where teacher forcing with the same encoder and recipe reaches 44.6 C@5 and on-policy state training 50.5. Teacher forcing alone thus already completes more chains on MuSiQue than every compared system (44.6 against 36.5 C@5 for Search-R1), and on the long-chain benchmarks it is far ahead of the graph-based systems and close to Search-R1 on HotpotQA-Long: a trained chain embedding retriever, which calls no language model at retrieval time, is a strong retriever for complex questions. The gain in complete coverage is larger than the gain in recall, which reflects what a chain needs: a question counts toward C@5 only when every step succeeds.

paragraphs.en: MuSiQue has at most four hops, while the long-chain benchmarks need up to five hops, or six to eight passages for comparisons, over corpora 19 to 48 times larger. The MuSiQue-trained encoder raises C@10 over the frozen encoder from 1.0 to 29.6 on HotpotQA-Long and from 2.0 to 32.8 on 2Wiki-Long. Search-R1 is the strongest competitor here. It puts fewer gold passages in its first five (C@5 3.3 and 6.0, against 20.8 and 27.7) but reaches a similar recall by the tenth passage, and leads on 2Wiki-Long in C@10. Its policy was trained with reinforcement learning on HotpotQA questions, from which part of HotpotQA-Long is built, and it spends a 7B forward pass per search. Our retriever uses a 0.6B encoder and one nearest neighbor search per step. The released MDR checkpoint, trained on HotpotQA, retrieves the most gold passages in the top five on HotpotQA-Long (51.0 R@5), but with two hops it completes few of the three- to five-hop chains (14.7 C@10, against 29.6).

paragraphs.en: Every component contributes, and the contributions grow on the longer chains. Removing the visited states, which leaves teacher forcing with the same encoder, recipe and number of states, costs 5.9 points of C@5 on MuSiQue and 5.7 and 10.4 points of C@10 on HotpotQA-Long and 2Wiki-Long. paragraphs.en: The diagnosis in Section 3 predicts where on-policy state training helps most: the states whose history already holds a wrong passage. paragraphs.en: We take the 3,403 states visited by the teacher-forced retriever that still miss a gold passage and let every encoder choose the next passage for them (Figure 3 b). On its own states, the teacher-forced encoder reproduces 99.8% of its recorded choices, so the probe matches retrieval. If on-policy state training only made the encoder better at retrieval in general, the gain would appear in clean states as well. It barely does: with a clean history, the three encoders succeed in 67.0%, 67.2% and 69.0% of the states. After one wrong passage, the rate rises from 25.0% under teacher forcing to 35.8% under on-policy state training, and after two or more from 14.5% to 29.2%, twice as often. Visited states collected once, without refresh, recover most of the way (32.2% and 25.1%). Because all encoders see the same states, the difference lies in the encoders themselves. The same pattern holds on the 3,352 states visited by the on-policy retriever: 66.8% against 68.5% with a clean history, 26.1% against 33.5% after one wrong passage and 20.0% against 24.2% after two or more.

paragraphs.en: To measure the effect of the contamination itself, we delete the non-gold passages from the contaminated states above and keep the gold ones in order; the deleted passages stay excluded from retrieval, as in the original state. On these 1,358 states, the teacher-forced encoder succeeds in 20.8% of the original states and in 32.1% once the wrong passages are removed: its own mistakes cost it 11.3 points. The on-policy encoder succeeds in 33.1% and 35.3%, so the same contamination costs it 2.2 points. Part of the low success after a mistake reflects harder states, since even the cleaned states stay well below the 67% of states that were clean to begin with. The rest is the effect of the wrong passages in the query, and on-policy state training removes most of it: on the contaminated states, the on-policy encoder (33.1%) does slightly better than the teacher-forced encoder does once an oracle has deleted the wrong passages (32.1%). It is also better on the cleaned states themselves (35.3% against 32.1%), which are gold histories with gaps, so part of the gain is skill on histories that skip a hop.

paragraphs.en: Figure 4 shows the same effect in the embedding space. We place each query vector by its similarity to the gold passages of the question and to the non-gold passages the two chains retrieve. The six questions share no gold passage and are the clearest of the 50 three- and four-hop questions on which our retriever finds every gold passage and the teacher-forced one misses at least one, ranked by the gap between the two retrievers in the softmax weight on the passage each should retrieve next and on non-gold passages. Once the teacher-forced chain retrieves a non-gold passage, its next query points at the non-gold passages and stays there, so the following steps retrieve more of them. Our query moves along the gold row hop by hop, and when it starts near non-gold passages (the fourth and fifth questions), it moves up to the gold row within one or two steps.

paragraphs.en: A cheaper explanation is that any contaminated history would do, as in training language models with distractor passages ( Yoran et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2024 ) . Table 4 separates the candidate explanations. Every row keeps half of the training states as gold states and changes the other half, under the same budget and recipe. Synthetic contamination inserts passages from the frozen encoder’s top 100 at random positions into gold histories, with the joint distribution of the number of wrong and gold passages matched to the visited states in aggregate (not per question or per epoch), and needs no roll-in; each synthetic state starts from a teacher-forced state with the drawn number of gold passages. It is either built once or resampled at every epoch. paragraphs.en: Table 4 shows three effects. First, contamination itself helps: synthetic contamination raises C@5 from 44.6 to 47.9, about half of the gap to on-policy state training. paragraphs.en: Chain embedding retrievers are trained on gold histories and run on their own retrievals. We showed that this gap is large in practice: by the third step, about half or more of the states a trained chain retriever visits contain one of its own mistakes, and these mistakes cost a teacher-forced encoder far more than the difficulty of the step explains. Training on the states the encoder visits, labeled with the earliest missing gold passage, changes this without a new architecture, objective or language model. The gain appears where the mismatch predicts, in recovery from contaminated histories, it depends on refreshing the visited states as the encoder learns, and it carries over to chains longer than those seen in training.

paragraphs.en: These results have three implications within the setting we study. First, the distribution of training states is a design choice for chain retrievers in addition to negatives and targets, and reporting how often test-time states leave that distribution would make results easier to interpret. Second, retrievers inside agents and reinforcement learning pipelines face the same mismatch, and dense supervision on visited states is a cheap complement to outcome rewards. Third, a trained chain embedding retriever, which needs no language model at retrieval time, is a strong baseline for graph-based and agentic retrieval for complex questions.
paragraphs.zh: 这些结果在我们所研究的情境下有三点启示。 首先，训练状态的分布是与负样本和目标样本并列的一个设计选择，报告测试时状态离开该分布的频率将使结果更易于解读。 其次，智能体和强化学习流程中的检索器面临同样的失配问题，对访问过的状态施加密集监督是结果奖励的一种低成本补充。 第三，训练好的链式嵌入检索器在检索时无需语言模型，是基于图的检索和面向复杂问题的智能体检索的一个强基线。

paragraphs.en: Of the 2,000 MuSiQue training questions, 200 are used for checkpoint selection. paragraphs.en: HippoRAG 2 and G-Retriever are run on a reduced corpus for each long-chain benchmark, a simpler setting than the full corpora. It contains all gold passages and the top 100 passages of every question under the frozen encoder (27,744 passages for HotpotQA-Long and 19,257 for 2Wiki-Long). paragraphs.en: 2Wiki-Long uses the evidence triples of 2WikiMultiHopQA as a graph over Wikidata entities, keeping only functional relations so that every hop has a single answer. Chains are paths of three to five hops in which every hop is supported by the paragraph of its subject entity, no entity repeats, and degenerate relation pairs (for example, the spouse of a mother) are excluded. Comparison questions map three or four entities through one relation to a person and then to a date, and ask which entity’s related person has the earliest or latest date. HotpotQA-Long starts from the two pages of an original bridge question and follows hyperlinks in the 2017 Wikipedia abstracts to reach three, four or five pages. Hops go only to named-entity pages with in-degree at most 300, through sentences with fewer than five links.
paragraphs.zh: 2Wiki-Long 将 2WikiMultiHopQA 的证据三元组用作 Wikidata 实体上的图，只保留函数性关系，使每一跳都有单一答案。 链是三到五跳的路径，其中每一跳都由其主体实体的段落所支持，实体不重复出现，并且排除退化的关系对（例如，母亲的配偶）。 比较类问题让三或四个实体通过同一关系映射到一个人，再映射到一个日期，然后询问哪个实体的相关人物具有最早或最晚的日期。 HotpotQA-Long 从原始桥接问题的两个页面出发，沿着 2017 年维基百科摘要中的超链接到达三、四或五个页面。 跳转只通过链接数少于五的句子，前往入度至多为 300 的命名实体页面。

paragraphs.en: A language model (deepseek-flash) writes one question per chain. The question may name only the starting entity, or the compared entities, and uses every relation in order. A question is kept only if it names no intermediate entity or answer, is answered correctly from the shuffled gold passages, is judged to have a unique answer, and is rated 4 or 5 for naturalness, all judged by the same model. A model of a different family (gpt-5.4-mini) then re-checks answerability and uniqueness; 62% of the 2Wiki-Long pool and 98% of the HotpotQA-Long pool pass. Questions whose final gold passage (for comparisons, all gold passages) appears in the top 10 of question-only BM25 over the final corpus are removed. Genealogy questions are capped at 40% of 2Wiki-Long, and question types are sampled evenly. HotpotQA-Long has 100 test questions each of three, four and five hops; 2Wiki-Long has 170, 45 and 12 chains of three, four and five hops and 73 comparison questions. The prompts are released with the benchmarks. Without passages, the reader of Section 5.2 answers 14.3% of the HotpotQA-Long and 14.7% of the 2Wiki-Long test questions, so the benchmarks require retrieval. Table 7 shows one test question of four types.

paragraphs.en: Beam decoding is a cheaper way to recover from an early mistake, so we decode both matched encoders with beams of two and four. Each beam is a partial chain scored by the sum of its similarities; at every step each beam expands its top candidates, the best partial chains are kept, and the passages of the best final chain are ranked first, followed by the maximum score of every passage over all encoded states. A beam of one is greedy decoding. Table 10 shows that beams improve teacher forcing by two to three points of complete coverage but leave a gap of four to six points, and that the greedy on-policy retriever outperforms the teacher-forced one with a beam of four, which encodes three times as many queries. Both encoders are those of Table 3 ; the re-encoded index moves greedy C@10 on HotpotQA-Long by one question.
paragraphs.zh: 束解码是一种代价更低的从早期错误中恢复的方法，因此我们用大小为二和四的束对两个匹配的编码器进行解码。 每个束都是由相似度之和评分的部分链；在每一步，每个束扩展其最优候选，保留最佳的部分链，最佳最终链的段落排在最前，其后是每个段落在所有编码状态上的最大得分。 大小为一的束就是贪心解码。 表 10 显示，束使教师强制的完全覆盖率提高二到三个百分点，但仍留有四到六个百分点的差距；并且贪心的在策略检索器优于使用大小为四的束的教师强制检索器，而后者编码的查询数量是前者的三倍。 两个编码器均为表 3 中的编码器；重新编码的索引使 HotpotQA-Long 上的贪心 C@10 提升了一个问题。
